subject: Post-demo: Shared capacity behavior profiling & SLO observability
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@avahealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya@avahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo: Shared capacity behavior profiling & SLO observability

Samir, Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment on the deployment concerns you raised (noisy neighbor, isolation guarantees, and how we measure SLOs when running on shared pools).

Key points from the call:
- Primary use case: inference for real-time triage + batch analytics. 90% of requests are short chats (~40 tokens) but with occasional long-context runs (~1k tokens).
- Concern: co-tenancy variance during business hours could cause tail-latency spikes that affect clinician experience.
- Preference ranking you gave: 1) Dedicated capacity with network isolation, 2) Private VPC if data residency required, 3) Hosted if strong SLO guarantees and fallbacks in place.
- Ops ask: visibility into per-tenant latency distribution and a simple way to detect noisy neighbor incidents automatically.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Share a short profiling checklist to capture your current traffic mix (attached).
2) Run a 2-week observability POC on our hosted pool with request-level tracing + a short synthetic load window to observe variability. We will provide dashboards and a recommended alert set.
3) If the variance is above your threshold, evaluate a small Dedicated pool (2 GPUs) for 2 weeks to compare behavior.

I attached a one-page mapping of Redwood observability metrics to SLO types (redwood-ops-slo-mapping.pdf) and a simple dataplane diagram that shows our interconnect options (ava-dataplane-diagram.png).

Can we lock in an ops profiling kickoff on Wednesday 16th at 16:00 ET? If that works, I’ll assign Marissa to the SLO config and Ben to the synthetic load run.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-ops-slo-mapping.pdf, ava-dataplane-diagram.png
From: Samir Rao <samir@avahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@avahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Shared capacity behavior profiling & SLO observability

Thanks, Logan — that summary is helpful. A couple of clarifying notes from our side: 

- We run a small but latency-sensitive clinician triage workflow between 09:00-18:00 ET. Anything over ~350ms P99 for <100 token responses would start to impact adoption.
- We can share anonymized traffic histograms and a sample of tail requests for your synthetic load generation.
- Data residency: currently hosted in GCP us-central; private VPC would be a later ask only if Dedicated doesn’t reduce variance enough.

We’re happy to do the Wednesday session but can we shorten it to 30 minutes — we want an ops-focused runbook and the synthetic window plan. Also: will the hosted POC give us tenant-level traces, or only aggregated pool metrics? That’s the key question for us.

- Samir
Director, Platform Engineering | Ava Health
ops@avahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@avahealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya@avahealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:46:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Shared capacity behavior profiling & SLO observability

Samir — quick answers so you can prep: 

- Tenant-level traces: during a hosted POC we enable request-level tracing tied to your tenant ID; we surface per-tenant latency distributions and the raw request sampling for forensic review (we retain samples for the POC window). We’ll not ingest sensitive payloads — only latency/headers and anonymized request sizes unless you opt-in to more detailed traces.
- Aggregates vs per-tenant: dashboards include both; alerts are configurable on per-tenant P99/P95 thresholds. We’ll provide a templated alert you can run in your pager on a trial basis.
- Synthetic plan: Ben will run a 30-minute burst where we ramp a synthetic client to mirror your worst-case concurrent users, then observe tail behavior for 30 minutes after ramp-down.

If Wednesday 16th at 16:00 ET is tight, we can also do 10:00 ET. Which do you prefer?

We’ll prepare a short ops runbook for the session (what we need from you, what we’ll do, expected artifacts).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: ops-runbook-template (we will upload ahead of the session)
From: Priya Menon <priya@avahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Shared capacity behavior profiling & SLO observability

Marissa / Logan — thanks. 10:00 ET works better for us on Wednesday. We’ll attach a small set of anonymized histograms and a JSON sample of long requests to the Drive folder you listed. For the tenant-level traces, we prefer the minimal sampling (latency + headers only) for the POC.

Action items from Ava: 
- Upload anonymized histograms + sample long-request JSON to the Drive link by end of day Tuesday.
- Confirm point of contact for the session: Samir will lead; Priya will support.

Action items from Redwood: 
- Share synthetic load script and a pre-configured alert template before the session (Marissa).
- Provide a side-by-side expected metric set so we can evaluate Dedicated if needed (Ben).

Looking forward to the call.

—Priya
Senior Engineering Manager | Ava Health
priay@avahealth.com
